Title: Predicting the Role of Political Trolls in Social Media
Technically, we leverage the community struc- ture and the text of the messages in the on- line social network of trolls represented as a graph, from which we extract several types of learned representations, i.e., embeddings, for the trolls. Social media have seen the prolifera- tion of fake news and clickbait (Hardalov et al., 2016; Karadzhov et al., 2017a), aggressiveness (Moore et al., 2012), and trolling (Cole, 2015). The latter often is understood to concern mali- cious online behavior that is intended to disrupt interactions, to aggravate interacting partners, and to lure them into fruitless argumentation in or- der to disrupt online interactions and communica- tion (Chen et al., 2013).

Predicting the Role of Political Trolls in Social Media Gianmarco De Francisci Morales Atanas Atanasov ISI Foundation Soﬁa University Bulgaria gdfm@acm.org amitkov@uni-sofia.bg Abstract We investigate the political roles of “Inter- arXiv:1910.02001v1 [cs.CL] 4 Oct 2019 net trolls” in social media. Political trolls, such as the ones linked to the Russian In- ternet Research Agency (IRA), have recently gained enormous attention for their ability to sway public opinion and even inﬂuence elections.

[11] Source: 1910.02001.pdf | Page: 2 | Section: None
Title: Predicting the Role of Political Trolls in Social Media
In particular, we use a combination of em- beddings built on the user-to-user mention graph, the user-to-hashtag mention graph, and the text of the tweets of the troll accounts. We further explore several possible approaches using label propaga- tion for the distant supervision scenario. As a result of our approach, we improve the classiﬁcation accuracy by more than 5 percent- age points for the supervised learning scenario.

answer: No, they do not only look at tweets. Besides the text of the tweets of the troll accounts, they also use embeddings built on the user-to-user mention graph and the user-to-hashtag mention graph [11]. More generally, they leverage the community structure and the text of the messages in the online social network of trolls represented as a graph, from which they extract several types of embeddings for the trolls [3][8].

question.reason: The supplied passages establish that the paper uses more than just tweets (mention graphs in addition to tweet text), answering the question.
